checks: Full-dimensional convexity gives positive volume to every nonempty open slab inside the support range. Ordinary cap profiles are strictly decreasing there, continuous including endpoints, and have constant tails. On any bounded t interval a common bounded tilt interval suffices because both cap traces are saturated for sufficiently large absolute tilt.

For t at or below the minimum split threshold, examine A mass greater than r, positive up to r, or zero. In the middle case the A threshold is its exact quantile; in the zero case the A threshold is at least its upper support. Both cases force the C threshold no higher than its matching quantile. The lower bound thus holds for every tilt.

At the minimum split use its two thresholds to get exact mass r. Above that threshold increase one component with positive mass and leave the other fixed. Since r<a≤c that mass is not full and strictly decreases. Strict inverse monotonicity is proved by scaling an optimizing split and continuity by compact normalized splits, which also identifies the positive plateau and zero tail.

Brunn–Minkowski supplies concavity of each ordinary cap root. Inverting a strictly decreasing concave function preserves concavity by reversing its comparison. The root split uses one common compact parameter set at every mass because a≤c. Pointwise infimum preserves the concave comparison. Invert the transition and extend left constantly using monotonicity; the right zero tail is excluded.

For the midpoint comparison, the equal positive split gives a threshold at least the minimizing split threshold. For r<K(t), this averaged threshold is at least t. The ordinary midpoint caps both have mass r/2, so actual midpoint inclusion and Brunn–Minkowski give r/2 in B at t. Letting r increase to K(t) includes its saturated value; the zero case is immediate.
The scope matches 35649ddf5df0135c §§1–3. No common measure is inferred across normals, and no concavity is asserted for the root of the sum with the middle cap.

overlap.comparison: It gives an explicit tilted-endpoint minimum in terms of a common-rank midpoint tail for the power-affine cone quantiles. The frozen theorem uses arbitrary convex endpoint caps and gives a general variational inverse and concavity, without that cone formula.
It compares actual endpoint masses with a comonotone midpoint law at a specified tilt. It neither minimizes the inverse split nor gives the power concavity of that minimum.

Its equal-capture proof gives an analogous midpoint upper bound at an all-normal attaining middle mark. The same equalization argument extends to each fixed normal and threshold and thus can prove this component independently. It does not provide the new split quantile or root concavity.

readability: The plateau and zero tail are separated from the strictly decreasing inverse. The positive set excludes the right zero tail.
review_method: Independent cold proof read on the frozen candidate, followed by original-scope and exact dependency comparison, with exact rational checks where applicable.
summary: The inverse-split formula, concavity of the optimized cap root, and the midpoint compatibility inequality all hold at the stated fixed normal.
